<thought>Using the ESI‑MS spectrum, the base peak at m/z 233.963 corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 232.956 Da. The strong M+2 peak (~24 % of the base) indicates the presence of a single chlorine atom (Cl‑35/Cl‑37 isotopic pattern). Removing the monoisotopic mass of Cl‑35 (34.96885 Da) leaves ≈ 197.987 Da to be accounted for by C, H, and O atoms. The combination C₁₁H₂O₄ matches this remaining mass within a few ppm. Adding the chlorine atom yields the molecular formula C₁₁H₂O₄Cl, which fits the observed exact mass and isotopic distribution.  

Therefore, the molecular formula of the compound is: C11H2O4Cl.
